ideas.risks: Standard Max-CSP hardness is usually proper or optimization hardness, not improper prediction hardness. If the example domain is polynomial, table learning kills the separation. Many approximation guarantees are additive in satisfaction rather than multiplicative in OPT, so the solver algebra may not apply without extra work.
ideas.summary: Try to instantiate the solver's approximation-gap template using assignment-induced concept classes from Max-CSP or related constraint systems. An explorer should write the exact learning reduction: examples are succinct constraint descriptions, concepts are assignments, labels are constraint truth values or noisy planted assignment values. Check whether an SDP/LP or other approximation algorithm gives err <= a OPT + xi, and whether OPT+epsilon improper prediction would imply a known hard task under a succinct-domain distribution.
ideas.title: CSP Approximation-Gap Instance
ideas.why_promising: This directly targets the new iteration-6 conditional route. CSPs are one of the few places where efficient constant approximations and hardness of near-optimal approximation coexist, so they are a natural source of a weak-but-not-strong separation candidate.

ideas.risks: Known correlation/potential boosters with additive slack leave a constant floor, and public-posterior obstructions may refute the needed low-OPT lemma. Anchor absorption is a serious threat for any small perturbation scheme.
ideas.summary: Analyze the most general public randomized relabeling/filtering scheme based on a current soft predictor F and the observed samples, not on the hidden comparator c. The goal is either to prove a lemma of the form 'if F has excess > epsilon, then some sampleable residual query has OPT_C < gamma and yields descent', or to construct a flat-posterior counterexample for the whole scheme class.
ideas.title: General Residual Low-OPT Lemma
ideas.why_promising: A positive result would bypass hidden clean tuple enumeration and give a real boosting route. A negative result would subsume several failed residual attempts and clarify exactly why fixed slack cannot be refined by public transformations.

ideas.risks: Even if final selection is solved, the hidden-clean bag generation and clean-population transfer bottlenecks remain. The extracted vote class may still contain agnostic halfspace selection as a special case, or the proof's margin may be too weak or empirical-only.
ideas.summary: Extract the exact final vote class in the da Cunha-Hogsgaard-Paudice proof: unrestricted real thresholds, nonnegative convex votes, bounded T-wise majorities, or something more structured. Then test whether the existence proof gives a margin or surrogate-risk certificate that enables polynomial-time selection over a generated bag, instead of enumerating all votes.
ideas.title: da Cunha Vote Selector
ideas.why_promising: The da Cunha route is the strongest positive near miss, and the final selector is a sharply isolated bottleneck. This direction can produce either a useful conditional positive theorem or a precise coordinate-bag hardness obstruction.

ideas.risks: The result may remain only a restricted oracle theorem rather than an atlas separation. Oracle outputs or hypothesis handles can leak enough information to make the bound vacuous, and low-OPT queries may be witnessed by public constants, spikes, or other concepts rather than the hidden target.
ideas.summary: Formalize a stopped-process public-posterior barrier. Define the public sigma-field generated by samples and allowed oracle replies, then bound the first time a smooth public filter or cell of mass mu has min(Pr[c(X)!=Y|G], Pr[c(X)=Y|G]) < gamma. Charge the event using the per-example KL lower bound and an explicit transcript information budget.
ideas.title: Stopped Public-Posterior Barrier
ideas.why_promising: It turns the strongest local obstructions from iterations 4-6 into a reusable theorem schema. Even if restricted, it would precisely diagnose which algorithms must create genuine clean-status information before fixed-slack weak calls become useful.

ideas.risks: Syntactic range can always be inflated by irrelevant encoded bits, while semantic population control may be impossible from black-box weak learning alone. Empirical clustering may not imply dual VC, stability, or clean-slice population guarantees for adaptive hidden-clean queries.
ideas.summary: Investigate whether an arbitrary efficient improper OPT+beta learner can be transformed into a controlled-range, stable, compressed, or canonical weak learner. Try sample splitting, repeated runs, validation-based pruning, empirical prediction clustering, and canonical tie-breaking. In parallel, build adversarial weak learners that satisfy the guarantee while forcing large semantic range or instability.
ideas.title: Regularize Weak Learners
ideas.why_promising: A positive result would feed directly into the conditional da Cunha theorem. A negative result would justify treating range, dual VC, compression, or stability as genuinely extra assumptions rather than artifacts of the known proof.

ideas.risks: Many candidates fail because low-noise weak learning is already computationally hard, or because known structure enables strong improper learning by validation/voting. The hardness must rule out arbitrary predictors, not just proper recovery or parameter identification.
ideas.summary: Search for represented classes where distribution-free weak learning is efficient whenever OPT_C < gamma, but agnostic improper learning at a larger noise rate eta > gamma is hard. Candidate families should be tested under Massart/malicious low-noise, random classification noise, and succinct-domain prediction, with special attention to avoiding finite-domain table learning.
ideas.title: Low-Noise Weak, Moderate-Noise Hard
ideas.why_promising: This attacks the hard band directly. For beta close to 1/2, the source only needs to work at very low noise, so a class with easy low-noise weak prediction but hard moderate-noise prediction would be a natural separation.
